appDescription: A long inland stage from the Nynäs/Humlenäs area to Lönhult. The route passes through Humlenäs naturreservat, follows the west side of meteorite lake Hummeln, crosses small roads and forest around Grytbäckskogen, continues through the old Bråbygden agricultural landscape, passes Bråhultsjön, Smisserum and the long stone wall known by hikers as the Småland 'Chinese wall', then reaches the Lönnebergaleden connection near Eckerhult before Lönhults kvarn and the Lönhult overnight cabin.

feesAsOfAccessedDate.notes: Same current Swedish/Naturkartan fee structure as Etapp 1; currentness-check before publication.

campingRules: Humlenäs reserve rules prohibit camping more than one day in the same place.
Tenting by Ostkustleden cabins has a 50 SEK/person fee according to current Swedish maintainer/Naturkartan pages.
Apply Swedish allemansrätten only outside protected areas/private yards and avoid tenting where it disturbs landowners, livestock, or cabin access.
fireRules: Humlenäs reserve permits fire only in own grill/outdoor stove or designated places.
Nynäs cabin page says no outdoor fires and no fire in the upstairs fireplace.
Lönhult cabin page says outdoor fires are not allowed at the cabin.
Bråhultsjöns badplats has a grill place, but it remains subject to current municipal/county fire bans.
Oskarshamn had no municipal fire ban at access time, but same-day fire-ban checks are required because status changes quickly.

protectedAreas.name: Humlenäs naturreservat / Natura 2000
rules: Drive only on roads and park only at designated parking.
Camp max one day in the same place.
Fire only in brought grill/outdoor stove or designated places.
Dogs and other pets must be leashed.
Do not disturb wildlife/nests/dens and do not damage trees, shrubs, fungi, mosses, or lichens without permission.

protectedAreas.name: Bråbygden Natura 2000 / LIFE RestoRED context
rules: Official Etapp 2 text says the route passes parts of Bråbygden; LIFE RestoRED identifies Bråbygden as Natura 2000 with ongoing grazing/restoration context.
Expect grazing, fencing, hamling/clearing context, and self-closing pedestrian gates in parts of Bråbygden.
Stay on the marked route, close gates, avoid disturbing livestock, keep dogs controlled/leashed near animals, and do not damage fences or trees.
protectedAreas.notes: Exact overlap between the Etapp 2 GPX and Bråbygden Natura 2000 polygons should be checked before publishing detailed protected-area wording.

waterProtection.name: Hummeln and Kristdala water source protection
waterProtection.notes: Relevant around Hummeln/Nynäs. Avoid washing, soap, greywater, fuel/chemical handling, or contamination near lake/streams; spills/leaks that risk pollution should be reported immediately.

hunting.notes: No Etapp 2-specific hunting notice was confirmed in the lane reports beyond broader Ostkustleden/Naturkartan seasonal elk-hunt notices seen elsewhere. Check the current section page and local signs before publication.

closuresAndCurrentness.notes: Nynäs page still shows a notice for forestry near the cabin during late summer/autumn 2025. Länsstyrelsen Humlenäs showed no current news in the lane report, so the notice may be stale but should be verified for 2026 before import.
No official Etapp 2 closure or reroute was found on Naturkartan, Döderhult, Oskarshamn, or Länsstyrelsen pages checked on 2026-04-29. Field signage may override web pages.

routeFinding.notes: Field reports and whole-route reviews indicate route-finding can be a real issue on or around Etapp 2. Use official GPX and current markings; third-party route-app data may be stale.

conditionReports.details: Section-specific report says the stage became over 25 km instead of about 21.5 km because of wrong turns and explicitly mentions route-finding problems. Also supports forest/gravel-road character, Bråhultsjön/Bråbo rest/bathing context, Smisserum's stone wall, Lönhults kvarn, and a two-car logistics pattern.
Two-stage Etapp 1-2 trip evidence describes the trip as wet and hard-going, but Etapp 2-specific detail is limited.
Club newsletter records Etapp 2 Nynäs-Lönhult walked on 2009-06-06, with a stop at Bråbo bathing place and no reported water/cabin/closure problem. Use as historical support only.
Whole-route review says cabins are excellent but the route can be hard to follow and the AllTrails route is an old version that may not match current marked trail. Not Etapp 2-specific.
First-six-sections review says the route is tough but varied, GPS/Google Maps was important, one unspecified section had missing yellow markers, and cabins were good.
Very old Nynäs concerns about smoky stove/chimney, low water, and variable cabin mattresses. Treat only as a prompt for current Nynäs verification, not as current condition.

sourceContradictions.details: Naturkartan page says 20.6 km, official GPX computes 20.622734 km, the official PDF map title says 21 km, Döderhult says cirka 22 km, and OSM/route-app lineage is around 21.5-21.6 km.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Use Naturkartan 20.6 km as current official section distance and keep computed geometry and alternates separate.

sourceContradictions.details: The official GPX start exactly matches the reviewed Etapp 1 digital endpoint, but Nynässtugan is about 565.9 m direct away and is reached by the GPX around route km 0.699.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Do not silently move the section start to the cabin. Decide endpoint policy at normalization, preserving both digital continuity and human-facing cabin metadata.

sourceContradictions.details: Older/maintainer wording says the well can dry in late summer; current Naturkartan wording says the well has dried and Hummeln water must always be boiled.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Treat Nynäs water as unreliable/unavailable and Hummeln as raw boil-required water pending local confirmation.

sourceContradictions.details: One agent report said Lönhult has no electricity and that water must be boiled, but main-thread checks of Naturkartan and Döderhult pages found electric power/electric hotplate and summer water at the cabin corner, with no current official boil-water wording located for Lönhult.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Use the current official page wording: electric hotplate/power and seasonal water. Do not present Lönhult water as reliable potable drinking water until potability is verified.

sourceContradictions.details: Official Naturkartan pages use Bråhultsjöns badplats / Bråhultesjön in text, while OSM may call parts of the same cluster Saxtorps badplats.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Use the official Bråhultsjöns badplats name and keep OSM/Saxtorp as secondary/source alias only.

sourceContradictions.details: Naturkartan Nynäs page still carries a late-summer/autumn 2025 forestry/RestoRED notice, while the rules lane found no current Länsstyrelsen Humlenäs news.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Keep as 2025 currentness risk and verify before presenting as an active 2026 condition.

sourceContradictions.details: Recent whole-route reviews warn that third-party app routes can be old or not match current markings.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Use official GPX as primary; use AllTrails/Gaia/Pacer only as condition/length cross-checks.

researchIterations.synthesisDecision: No second agent batch spawned. Official distance, geometry, endpoint coordinates, commute access, major facilities, rules/safety, and field-currentness evidence are sufficient for research-ready handoff. Remaining issues are explicit import/normalization caveats rather than blockers to completing this section packet.

researchIterations.activity: Main thread rechecked Naturkartan Etapp 2, Nynäs cabin, Lönhult cabin, Bråhultsjöns badplats, Lönhults kvarn, and Döderhult overview pages to resolve facility wording conflicts before writing the section JSON.
researchIterations.synthesisDecision: Official Lönhult page wording overrides the lane conflict: record electric hotplate/power and seasonal water at the cabin corner, but keep water potability/currentness pending.

Is the Nynäs cabin offset an intentional stage-chaining choice, a map export artifact, or an access spur that should be modeled separately?
Is the Nynäs well permanently dry, seasonally dry, or restored after the current Naturkartan wording?
Are any 2025 forestry/RestoRED works around Nynäs/Humlenäs still affecting route access or signage in 2026?
What is the exact coordinate for the small signed bathing place in Humlenäs reserve?
Does Etapp 2 GPX intersect Bråbygden Natura 2000 polygons, and exactly where should livestock/gate/restoration caveats be attached?
What is the exact coordinate and current potability status of the Lönhult summer-water tap?
Should the Småland 'Chinese wall' near Smisserum be imported as a POI, and can an official coordinate be found?
Can KLT current planner data confirm practical regular-bus versus pre-booked Närtrafik access for Lönhult at publication time?
Are there current local hunting/forestry signs near Grytbäckskogen, Eckerhult, or Lönhult that are not reflected on web pages?

blockingIssues: Nynäs endpoint policy must be decided before route import so the app does not hide the GPX/cabin offset.
Lönnebergaleden connector must be modelled separately from main Etapp 2 geometry.
Seasonal/currentness details for Lönhult water and Nynäs water/forestry need confirmation before user-facing availability claims.
Some optional POIs have approximate or OSM-only coordinates and should remain pending/suppressed during normalization.
Fire-ban, transit schedule, and hunting/forestry notices are time-sensitive.

At later normalization, import Etapp 2 from official Naturkartan GPX, keep Nynäs endpoint ambiguity visible, dedupe Nynäs cabin/toilet with Etapp 1, import high-confidence Bråhultsjön and Lönhult facilities, and model Lönnebergaleden as connector metadata.
